threads.body: extract_floor_version() currently returns min(floors). For specifier sets with multiple lower-bound constraints (e.g. ">= 1.0" and ">= 1.1"), the effective floor is the *maximum* lower bound; using min can mis-compute the floor and cause false failures/passes in the editable-oldest check.

threads.body: The editable-oldest validation only checks `floor < min_v`. This won’t catch the key mismatch the check is meant to enforce: a dependency like `>= 1.1b0` (release) will pass even when the editable package’s current version is `1.1b0.dev…`, because `1.1b0` compares greater than `1.1b0.dev0` but does *not* actually allow installing the dev version. Consider additionally verifying that `min_v` itself satisfies the requirement’s specifier set (with prereleases enabled).

threads.body: This test module mutates `sys.path` at import time and never restores it, which can leak into other tests (and change import resolution order). It’s safer to remove the inserted path after importing `check_deps` so the rest of the test session runs with the normal sys.path ordering.
